title: [YouPass Collect] - Home Smokery System
prompt: The diagram below describes the structure of a home smokery and how it works. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The diagram illustrates the structure of a home smokery and demonstrates the process by which fish is smoked using this apparatus.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the smoking process consists of three main stages that work in sequence to transform fresh fish into smoked fish. The system operates by drawing fresh air through a fire chamber before directing the resulting smoke into a storage box containing the fish.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: The process begins at stage 1, where fresh air enters the system through an opening that can be controlled by a lid mechanism. This fresh air then flows downward into stage 2, which houses the fire chamber located underground. In this chamber, wood is burned to generate both heat and smoke, with the lid providing control over airflow to maintain optimal burning conditions.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: The smoke produced in stage 2 is subsequently channeled through a pipe that leads to stage 3, where the actual smoking takes place. This final stage consists of a box positioned at ground level, which contains the fish to be smoked. The smoke enters the box through the connecting pipe, allowing it to circulate around the fish and impart the desired smoky flavor. The box appears to have a lid for easy access and to contain the smoke during the smoking process.
